exercise.name: Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise
aliases: Seated one-leg heel raise with dumbbell

reference.title: Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise
reference.listing: Page could not be read (blocked by the network proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the heel rises, inhale as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.0 s up, 0.8 s pause, 1.8 s down

prescription.tempo: 1-1-2-0 (1 s up, 1 s pause, 2 s down)
prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3). One leg takes the whole dumbbell, so start lighter than half of your two-leg seated load times two.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a heavier dumbbell; a plate under the ball of the foot adds range.

cues.text: Sit tall on the end of a bench, feet flat, shins vertical; rest a dumbbell across the lower right thigh just behind the knee and hold it there, left hand on the left thigh.
Breathe out and push through the ball of the right foot, lifting the heel as high as you can.
Pause at the top and squeeze the calf; keep the pressure over the big toe.
Breathe in and lower the heel slowly until the foot is flat.
Heel down, brief reset; switch legs after the set.

mistakes.fix: Lower slowly and pause at both ends.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing the dumbbell up with the arm
mistakes.fix: The hand only steadies the dumbbell; the calf lifts it.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling onto the outside of the foot
mistakes.fix: Keep the pressure over the big toe.
Rise as high as you can and lower until the foot is flat.

kinematics.norm: Full range from the flat foot to the highest heel position (clinical opinion)
Several centimetres of heel rise; as high as you can (clinical opinion)
Knee bent about 90 degrees: with the knee bent the soleus does more of the work than the gastrocnemius (Hébert-Losier 2012)
Across the lower thigh just behind the knee, steadied by the hand (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up, a short pause, 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #1901, Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise, animation (movement reference; page not readable here)
Hébert-Losier, Schneiders, García, Sullivan & Simoneau 2012, influence of knee flexion angle and age on triceps surae muscle fatigue during heel raises (J Strength Cond Res 26(11))
Kinoshita, Maeo et al. 2023, triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training (Front Physiol 14:1272106)

cautions: Use a towel or pad under the dumbbell if the handle presses into the thigh.
Keep the dumbbell steady with the hand so it cannot roll off the thigh onto the foot.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Achilles or calf discomfort: shorten the range and slow down.
progressions: Ball of the foot on a plate or step for more range.

muscleNotes.calves_r: Lifts the heel; with the knee bent the soleus contributes more than the gastrocnemius (Hébert-Losier 2012). Seated calf-raise training grew the soleus but not the gastrocnemius in Kinoshita 2023.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the dumbbell steady on the thigh.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk upright on the bench.

phases.label: Rise onto the ball of the foot

guides.label: Heel up, then all the way down
